newsitem.title: HONDURAS: One shot in new Honduras prison riot.
newsitem.headline: One shot in new Honduras prison riot.

text.p: A new prison riot erupted in Honduras on Wednesday as police and soldiers searched for 232 inmates who escaped from another jail that was set on fire earlier in the week, authorities said.
The latest riot, the third in three days, broke out in the southeastern city of Danli, injuring two inmates, one of whom was shot by a guard, police said.
"Everything is now under control," Danli police chief Maj. Dagoberto Cruz told Reuters. "The central jail is under the protection of the police."

The violence has underscored the wretched conditions for prisoners in Honduras, where 24 jails are packed beyond twice their intended capacity and 92 percent of inmates have yet to be formally sentenced.
Monday's mass escape has led to concern in areas near the prison.
"I'm scared that they might try to break in here and steal things," Ana Lopez, a maid in the town of Santa Barbara, said in a telephone interview.
Legislators, meanwhile, called on Wednesday for a firmer government hand in clamping down on the violence.
"The government should order the militarization of the jails to avoid these bloody and uncontrollable riots," said Oscar Avila, vice president of the National Congress.
Opposition Congressman Raul Pineda complained that "the wardens no longer run the prisons in Honduras, the inmates do."
Inmates in Santa Barbara on Monday set fire to the jail and 482 of them got away in the intial confusion. The town of about 35,000 people is 110 miles (180 kms) northwest of Tegucigalpa, the capital.
Authorities said 250 inmates had been rounded up while 600 army troops and police officers searched for the rest.
Inmates also rioted and set fire to another jail on Monday in the town of Trujillo, 180 miles (290 km) north of the capital, but officials said no prisoners had escaped or were injured.
Wednesday's uprising took place among 311 prisoners in Danli, some 60 miles (100 kms) east of Tegucigalpa near the Nicaraguan border.

"The people rioted because they heard the warden say that the inmates don't need a pardon," a prisoner, identified as Jorge Lopez, told HRN radio station. "They started to throw sticks and stones and the guards opened fire, injuring two."
